questions.question: Which Indian state topped the 'Environment' theme in the State of States rankings of the State of India’s Environment 2025 report released by the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Himachal Pradesh** has been recognized as the top-performing state under the **'Environment' theme** in the **State of India’s Environment 2025 report**, published by the **Centre for Science and Environment (CSE)**.
 
• The report evaluates states based on their environmental initiatives, including **forest conservation, pollution control, renewable energy adoption, and biodiversity preservation**.
 
• Himachal Pradesh has excelled in areas such as **forest cover preservation** and the implementation of **environment-friendly policies**, earning high rankings in terms of sustainable development.
 
• Key initiatives in Himachal Pradesh include a significant focus on **hydropower projects**, **afforestation programs**, and policies aimed at minimizing **plastic waste**.
 
• The state’s proactive measures to **mitigate climate change** and promote **green energy** have made it a model for environmental sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Centre for Science and Environment (CSE):**

 
 
• The **CSE** is a public interest research and advocacy organization based in India that focuses on sustainable development and environmental conservation.
 
• It publishes the **State of India’s Environment report**, which assesses the environmental performance of states based on diverse indicators such as air quality, water management, forest cover, and climate action.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh’s Environmental Achievements:**
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh is known for its **high forest cover**, accounting for approximately **66.52% of its geographical area**, as per the **India State of Forest Report (ISFR)**.
 
• The state has implemented a **plastic ban** policy, making it one of the first states in India to take stringent measures against plastic pollution.
 
• Hydropower contributes significantly to the state’s energy needs, with Himachal Pradesh being a leader in **renewable energy adoption**.
 
• The state has introduced programs such as ** to promote environmental sustainability and biodiversity conservation.
 
 
 
• State of India’s Environment Report:**
 
 
• The **State of India’s Environment 2025 report** provides a comprehensive evaluation of state performances on various themes like health, education, environment, and governance.
 
• The report is widely recognized for encouraging states to adopt **sustainable practices** and improve their environmental policies.
 
• It highlights the importance of balancing **economic development** with **environmental conservation**.
 
 
 
• **Other States Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh:** Known for its focus on **agriculture and irrigation projects**, but it has faced challenges in forest cover management.
 
• **Uttar Pradesh:** Faces environmental issues such as **air and water pollution**, with efforts being made to improve waste management systems.
 
• **Madhya Pradesh:** Features a significant forest cover but has struggled with industrial pollution and urbanization challenges.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Forest Cover in India:**

 
 
• India’s total forest and tree cover is estimated at **24.62% of its geographical area**, as per the **ISFR 2021**.
 
• States like **Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, and Himachal Pradesh** have high percentages of forest cover relative to their total area.
 
 
 
• **Plastic Waste Management:**
 
 
• India generates approximately **3.5 million tons of plastic waste** annually.
 
• Himachal Pradesh’s plastic ban policy serves as a model for reducing plastic waste in other states.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy Initiatives:**
 
 
• India is the third-largest producer of **renewable energy**, with states like Himachal Pradesh leading in **hydropower generation**.
 
• Renewable energy accounts for approximately **40% of India’s installed electricity capacity**.

questions.question: How many prototypes of the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) does India plan to develop before starting series production?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India plans to develop five prototypes** of the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) before initiating series production. This development strategy ensures thorough testing and validation of the aircraft's design and functionality.
 
• The AMCA is a **fifth-generation fighter aircraft** project undertaken by India. It aims to enhance the nation's air combat capabilities significantly.
 
• The development of prototypes is crucial to identifying and resolving design flaws, optimizing performance, and ensuring operational readiness for mass production.
 
• The AMCA is being developed under the aegis of the **Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA)** in collaboration with other key stakeholders, such as Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL).
 
• Prototype development is an integral part of the aircraft manufacturing process. It allows engineers and scientists to test the aircraft under varying conditions, ensuring compliance with operational requirements and safety standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA):**

 
 
• The AMCA is a **stealth, multi-role fighter aircraft** designed for superior aerial combat, precision strike missions, and ground attack capabilities.
 
• This indigenous project is part of India's efforts to reduce dependence on foreign defense equipment and achieve self-reliance in defense technology.
 
• The AMCA will feature advanced technologies such as **stealth capabilities, supercruise, and advanced avionics systems**.
 
• The aircraft will be powered by twin engines and is expected to have a maximum takeoff weight of approximately **25 tons**.
 
• The AMCA will be equipped with state-of-the-art weaponry, including **long-range missiles, smart munitions, and electronic warfare systems**.
 
 
 
• **Prototype Development Process:**
 
 
• Prototype development involves creating a preliminary version of the aircraft to test its design and functionality.
 
• Through rigorous testing, engineers identify and rectify issues related to performance, safety, and reliability.
 
• The prototype phase is essential for ensuring the aircraft meets operational requirements and adheres to international standards.
 
• After successful testing, the design is finalized, and the aircraft progresses to series production for deployment.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Fifth-Generation Fighter Aircraft:**
 
 
• Fifth-generation aircraft are characterized by **stealth technology**, making them less detectable by radar and infrared systems.
 
• They incorporate **supercruise capability**, enabling sustained supersonic flight without afterburners.
 
• These aircraft are equipped with advanced **avionics and sensors** for enhanced situational awareness.
 
• They possess superior maneuverability, which is crucial for air combat dominance.
 
• Examples of fifth-generation fighters include the **F-22 Raptor** and **Su-57 Felon**.
 
 
 
• **India’s Defense Initiatives:**
 
 
• India has been actively pursuing indigenous defense projects under the **‘Make in India’ initiative**.
 
• Other significant projects include the **Tejas Light Combat Aircraft (LCA)** and various missile systems.
 
• These efforts aim to reduce dependency on foreign defense imports and enhance India’s strategic autonomy.
 
• India’s defense sector also emphasizes collaboration with private industries and international partners for technology sharing and co-development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Timeline of AMCA Development:**

 
 
• The AMCA project was conceptualized to replace older aircraft like the **MIG-21** and **Jaguar**.
 
• The first prototype is expected to be ready by **2024-2025**, with series production likely to begin by **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Collaborations:**
 
 
• The project is being jointly developed by the **Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA)** and **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)**.
 
• International partnerships for critical technologies, such as **engine development**, are also being explored.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• The AMCA will significantly boost India’s air defense capabilities and reduce reliance on foreign fighter jets like the **Rafale**.
 
• It will also enhance India’s position as a defense exporter, supporting allied nations with cutting-edge technology.

• The **2025 edition** of the VARUNA exercise was held in **March 2025**, showcasing joint maneuvers, tactical operations, and maritime drills.
 
• This exercise includes activities such as surface and anti-submarine warfare, air defense operations, and joint naval maneuvers.

• Both countries collaborate extensively to ensure **maritime security** in the **Indo-Pacific region**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1: MITRA**

 
 
• This is not related to any bilateral naval exercise between India and France.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: VARUNA**
 
 
• Correct answer: The name of the bilateral naval exercise between the **Indian Navy** and the **French Navy**.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: EKUVERIN**
 
 
• A joint military exercise between **India and the Maldives**.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: DOSTANA**

questions.question: World Environment Day was observed on 5 June 2025 with a special focus to end which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plastic Pollution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Environment Day** is celebrated every year on **5th June**, and in 2025, the theme focused on addressing **Plastic Pollution**, a global environmental challenge.
 
• **Plastic Pollution** has devastating effects on ecosystems, marine life, terrestrial habitats, and human health due to its **non-biodegradable nature** and accumulation in the environment.
 
• As part of the **2025 observance**, countries worldwide emphasized reducing single-use plastics and transitioning to **sustainable alternatives**.
 
• The initiative aligned with the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)** campaign titled "**Beat Plastic Pollution**" to promote policies, awareness, and actions to curb the menace of plastic waste.
 
• Efforts were concentrated on enhancing **recycling infrastructure**, encouraging biodegradable materials, and implementing stringent regulations to minimize plastic usage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Plastic Pollution:**

 
 
• **Definition:** The accumulation of plastic objects and particles (e.g., bottles, bags, microplastics) adversely affects the environment, wildlife, and human health.
 
• **Sources:** Major contributors include **single-use plastics**, packaging materials, and improperly disposed plastic waste.
 
• **Statistics:** According to UNEP, **over 400 million tons of plastic** are produced annually, of which only **less than 10%** is recycled.
 
• **Impact:** Plastics pollute oceans, leading to the death of marine species, disrupt soil fertility, and release toxic chemicals during degradation.
 
 
 
• **Global Efforts to Combat Plastic Pollution:**
 
 
• **United Nations Initiatives:** UNEP launched the "**Beat Plastic Pollution**" campaign to address the global crisis.
 
• **Policy Actions:** Nations have introduced bans on single-use plastics, imposed taxes on plastic products, and promoted circular economy models.
 
• **Innovations:** Research is being conducted into **biodegradable plastics**, and businesses are transitioning to **eco-friendly materials**.
 
 
 
• **Alternatives to Plastic:**
 
 
• **Biodegradable Materials:** Such as bamboo, jute, paper, and organic polymers.
 
• **Reusable Products:** Promotion of steel, glass, and cloth-based alternatives for packaging and storage.
 
• **Recycling:** Advanced technologies to recycle plastic waste efficiently.
 
 
 
• **Role of Individuals:**
 
 
• Adopting **zero-waste lifestyles** by minimizing plastic usage in daily activities.
 
• Participating in **clean-up drives** and supporting awareness campaigns.
 
• Opting for products made from **sustainable materials**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP):**

 
 
• The **UNEP** has been instrumental in leading global efforts against plastic pollution through initiatives and partnerships.
 
• Its campaigns focus on sustainable waste management, marine conservation, and promoting eco-friendly alternatives.
 
 
 
• **Global Reports:**
 
 
• The **Global Plastic Pollution Report** highlights that plastic waste contributes to **80% of marine debris**, affecting over **700 marine species**.
 
• Studies emphasize the need for **global cooperation** in combating plastic pollution, citing rapid increases in production and disposal rates.
 
 
 
• **Government Regulations:**
 
 
• Several countries, including **India, Kenya, and the EU**, have implemented bans on single-use plastics and set recycling targets.
 
• Policies promoting **Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)** ensure manufacturers manage post-consumer waste.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as Executive Director of the Reserve Bank of India in March 2025 to look after Department of Statistics and Information Management and Financial Stability Department?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Ajit Ratnakar Joshi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Ajit Ratnakar Joshi** was appointed as the **Executive Director** of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **March 2025**.
 
• He is responsible for overseeing two critical departments of the RBI:
 
 
• The **Department of Statistics and Information Management (DSIM)**, which handles statistical analysis, data collection, and information management to support RBI's policy decisions.
 
• The **Financial Stability Department (FSD)**, which ensures the stability of India's financial system by identifying and mitigating systemic risks.
 
 
 
• **Dr. Ajit Ratnakar Joshi** is known for his extensive experience in economics, finance, and data analysis, making him well-suited for these vital roles in RBI.
 
• His appointment aligns with RBI's objective of strengthening its analytical and data-driven approach to policy formulation and maintaining financial stability in India.
 
• He has previously held important positions in various financial institutions and is recognized for his contributions to economic policymaking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the central banking institution of India, responsible for regulating the country's monetary policy and ensuring financial stability.
 
• It was established on **1 April 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• The RBI performs functions such as issuing currency, managing foreign exchange reserves, regulating and supervising banks, and acting as the banker to the government.
 
 
 
• **Department of Statistics and Information Management (DSIM):**
 
 
• This department collects, compiles, and analyzes macroeconomic and financial statistics critical for policymaking.
 
• It also develops statistical methodologies and manages the digital infrastructure for data storage and dissemination.
 
• The DSIM is instrumental in conducting surveys, such as the Consumer Confidence Survey and Inflation Expectations Survey, which aid the RBI in decision-making.
 
 
 
• **Financial Stability Department (FSD):**
 
 
• Established in 2010, the FSD is tasked with monitoring the stability of India's financial system.
 
• It identifies systemic risks, conducts stress testing, and formulates measures to prevent financial crises.
 
• The department also publishes the **Financial Stability Report**, which provides a comprehensive assessment of the health of the financial sector.
 
 
 
• **Executive Directors in RBI:**
 
 
• Executive Directors (EDs) play a pivotal role in implementing RBI's policies and managing its various departments.
 
• They typically have extensive experience in banking, finance, economics, or related fields and are responsible for key operational areas of the central bank.
 
• The appointment of EDs is crucial for ensuring effective governance and operational efficiency within the RBI.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **RBI** is headquartered in **Mumbai** and has multiple regional offices across India.
 
• The **Governor** of RBI is the chief executive officer, supported by Deputy Governors and Executive Directors.
 
• In recent years, the RBI has emphasized the importance of data-driven decision-making to enhance policy effectiveness and transparency.
 
• The **Financial Stability Report (FSR)**, published semi-annually by the FSD, provides key insights into the health of the banking and financial sectors.
 
• The DSIM has been at the forefront of modernizing statistical practices and adopting advanced data analytics to support the RBI's regulatory and supervisory functions.

questions.question: In June 2025, the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, convened a high-level meeting co-chaired by M Nagaraju, Secretary, Department of Financial Services and T Rabi Sankar, Deputy Governor, RBI at New Delhi, on scaling up ULI. What is the full form of ULI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unified Lending Interface**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Unified Lending Interface (ULI)** refers to a unified platform that aims to streamline and simplify the lending processes by integrating different financial stakeholders, including banks, non-banking financial institutions, and regulatory bodies.
 
• The **Department of Financial Services (DFS)** under the **Ministry of Finance**, along with the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, convened a high-level meeting in **June 2025** to discuss scaling up ULI.
 
• This initiative is expected to enhance transparency, improve credit accessibility, and increase efficiency in the lending ecosystem for borrowers and lenders alike.
 
• The meeting was co-chaired by **M Nagaraju**, Secretary, Department of Financial Services, and **T Rabi Sankar**, Deputy Governor of RBI, reflecting the collaboration between government departments and regulatory institutions.
 
• ULI may potentially utilize advanced technologies like **blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), and digital interfaces** to ensure seamless integration across financial platforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Department of Financial Services (DFS):**

 
 
• The DFS operates under the **Ministry of Finance**, Government of India, and is responsible for overseeing various financial institutions including banks, insurance companies, and pension schemes.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in formulating policies to improve financial inclusion and strengthen India's financial ecosystem.
 
• Key initiatives under DFS include schemes like **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana** and **Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana**.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**
 
 
• The RBI is India's central banking institution, established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• It regulates monetary policy, manages foreign exchange reserves, and ensures the stability of the financial system in India.
 
• Key functions include issuing currency, managing inflation, and supervising banks and non-banking financial institutions.
 
 
 
• **Unified Lending Interface (ULI) Features:**
 
 
• ULI aims to integrate various lending platforms for improved coordination and efficiency.
 
• It is expected to provide a **centralized database** for lenders, enabling easier credit assessments and reducing loan processing times.
 
• The interface could support **digital KYC** and **real-time credit scoring**, ensuring better transparency.
 
• It may also help reduce fraudulent activities by cross-verifying borrower details through unified digital frameworks.
 
 
 
• **Future Implications of ULI:**
 
 
• With enhanced integration, ULI could serve as a **game-changer for small businesses and individuals** seeking easier access to credit.
 
• The introduction of ULI aligns with India's broader goals of **digital transformation** and financial inclusion.
 
• It could provide opportunities for innovative lending solutions such as **peer-to-peer lending** and **microcredit systems**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Integration:** The success of ULI will depend on the implementation of advanced technologies like **blockchain** for secure data sharing and **AI** for predictive credit scoring.
 
• **Policy Alignment:** ULI must align with existing financial policies and regulations to ensure smooth implementation and compliance.
 
• **Stakeholder Collaboration:** Effective collaboration among banks, NBFCs, and fintech companies is critical for the success of ULI.
 
• **Impact on Financial Inclusion:** ULI could significantly improve access to credit for underserved sectors, including rural and semi-urban areas.
 
• **Monitoring and Evaluation:** Regular performance assessments will be crucial to measure the effectiveness of ULI and make necessary improvements.

questions.question: Who is the Chairperson of the 16th Finance Commission of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arvind Panagariya**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **N. K. Singh** was the Chairperson of the **15th Finance Commission** and is a notable economist and policymaker in India.
 
• The **16th Finance Commission** has been constituted as of the latest updates. The Chairperson of the 16th Finance Commission of India is Dr. Arvind Panagariya. 
 
• The Chairperson of a Finance Commission is typically an expert in public finance, economics, or administration, ensuring that the recommendations align with national priorities.
 
• **N. K. Singh**, as the Chairperson of the 15th Finance Commission, played a significant role in addressing critical financial issues such as **tax devolution, grants to local bodies, and disaster management funds.**
 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under **Article 280 of the Indian Constitution**, which ensures a sound fiscal relationship between the **Union and the States.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Finance Commission:**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is a **constitutional body** constituted by the President of India every **five years** under **Article 280**.
 
• Its primary function is to recommend the division of **tax revenues** between the **Union and the States** and among the states themselves.
 
• It also addresses issues related to **grants-in-aid** for local bodies and other financial matters as referred to it by the President.
 
 
 
• **Key Responsibilities of the Chairperson:**
 
 
• To lead discussions on **fiscal policies** and ensure equitable revenue sharing between the Union and States.
 
• To analyze and address economic challenges, such as **fiscal deficits, state debts, and revenue mobilization.**

questions.question: India is drafting its first comprehensive framework, National Adaptation Plan (NAP), to be submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) by September 2025 in compliance with the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Paris Agreement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's National Adaptation Plan (NAP)** is being drafted as the country’s first comprehensive framework for climate adaptation to address challenges posed by **climate change**.
 
• The **Paris Agreement**, adopted in **December 2015**, mandates signatory countries to submit their National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) to the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**.
 
• The Paris Agreement specifically aims to limit global temperature rise to **below 2°C above pre-industrial levels** and pursue efforts to limit the temperature increase to **1.5°C**.
 
• Under the Paris Agreement, countries are expected to focus not only on **mitigation** (reducing greenhouse gas emissions) but also on **adaptation** strategies to build resilience against climate impacts.
 
• India’s NAP is set to be submitted by **September 2025**, demonstrating India's compliance with its international climate commitments under the Paris Agreement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Paris Agreement:**

 
 
• The Paris Agreement is a landmark international treaty adopted during the **21st Conference of Parties (COP21)** in Paris, France.
 
• It involves commitments by **196 parties** to combat climate change and adapt to its effects, with enhanced support to assist developing countries.
 
• The agreement includes provisions for **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**, where countries outline their climate actions and targets.
 
• It emphasizes global financial support for adaptation initiatives, especially in developing countries.
 
• The agreement entered into force on **4 November 2016**.
 
 
 
• **Cartagena Protocol:**
 
 
• Adopted in **2000** as a supplementary agreement to the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)**.
 
• Focuses on the safe handling, transport, and use of living modified organisms (LMOs) resulting from modern biotechnology.
 
• It does not address climate change but rather biodiversity and biosafety issues.
 
 
 
• **Kyoto Protocol:**
 
 
• Adopted in **1997**, it aimed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions globally, primarily focusing on industrialized nations.
 
• It set binding emission reduction targets but was replaced by the Paris Agreement as it failed to engage all nations equally.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol:**
 
 
• Adopted in **1987**, this protocol focuses on protecting the ozone layer by phasing out ozone-depleting substances.
 
• It is not related to climate adaptation plans but is considered one of the most successful environmental treaties.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India’s Climate Commitments:**

 
 
• India submitted its **NDCs** under the Paris Agreement, pledging to reduce its emissions intensity of GDP by **33-35% by 2030** compared to 2005 levels.
 
• It also aims to achieve **40% of its electric power capacity** from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030.
 
 
 
• **National Adaptation Plan (NAP):**
 
 
• The NAP process is critical for developing countries to enhance resilience against climate impacts.
 
• It involves comprehensive research, stakeholder consultations, and policy framing to mitigate vulnerabilities.
 
 
 
• **UNFCCC:**
 
 
• The UNFCCC was established in **1992** to combat climate change and its impacts globally.
 
• The Paris Agreement operates under the framework of the UNFCCC.

questions.question: On 20th May, 2025, the Supreme Court (SC) reinstated the requirement of how many years of legal practice for law graduates to apply for civil judge (junior division) posts, reversing its 2002 decision?
questions.solution:

__
 
• On **20th May, 2025**, the Supreme Court of India reinstated the requirement of **3 years** of legal practice for law graduates to apply for the posts of **Civil Judge (Junior Division).**
 
• This decision reversed a previous ruling made by the Supreme Court in **2002**, which had allowed fresh law graduates to directly apply for these judicial posts without any mandatory legal practice.
 
• The **3-year legal practice requirement** ensures that candidates gain adequate exposure and experience in the field of law before assuming judicial responsibilities.
 
• The move aligns with the objective of enhancing the quality of judicial appointments and ensuring that candidates have substantial practical knowledge of legal proceedings.
 
• The Supreme Court emphasized the importance of practical experience in law to ensure candidates are well-prepared to handle judicial duties effectively. ***Hence, the correct answer is 3 years.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Supreme Court's 2002 Decision:**

 
 
• In **2002**, the Supreme Court allowed law graduates to apply for Civil Judge posts without requiring prior legal practice.
 
• This decision was aimed at increasing the pool of candidates for judicial posts and fast-tracking appointments.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Legal Practice:**
 
 
• Legal practice enables candidates to gain **hands-on experience** in court proceedings, drafting, arguing cases, and understanding nuances of legal processes.
 
• It also helps candidates develop critical thinking, analytical skills, and familiarity with judicial ethics and responsibilities.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility for Civil Judge (Junior Division):**

• Post the Supreme Court’s 2025 ruling, candidates must have **3 years of legal practice** as a prerequisite.
 
• Age limits and other criteria may vary across states in India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Judicial Appointments:**

• Experienced and well-trained judges contribute to maintaining the quality, impartiality, and integrity of the judiciary.

• The Supreme Court of India is the **highest judicial authority** in the country and has the power to interpret laws and review its previous decisions.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in ensuring justice and upholding the **Constitution of India.**
 
 
 
• **Judicial Ethics and Experience:**
 
 
• Judicial ethics demand fairness, impartiality, and adherence to legal principles.
 
• Practical legal experience equips candidates with skills to manage complex cases and deliver unbiased decisions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Decision:**
 
 
• The reinstatement of the **3-year legal practice requirement** aims to enhance the competency of Civil Judges (Junior Division).
 
• It ensures that candidates have sufficient exposure to real-world legal challenges before taking on judicial roles.

questions.question: Which country was ranked highest for gender equality in the Global Gender Gap Report, 2025, released by the World Economic Forum in May 2025?

__
 
• **Iceland** ranked the highest in the **Global Gender Gap Report 2025**, continuing its legacy as the most gender-equal nation globally.
 
• Iceland has been consistently performing well in gender equality metrics such as **economic participation, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment**.
 
• The nation has achieved nearly **91.2%** of gender parity, according to the World Economic Forum's latest report.
 
• Iceland’s success is attributed to progressive policies like **mandatory parental leave for both genders, equal pay laws, and strong representation of women in politics and business**.
 
• The **Global Gender Gap Report**, published by the **World Economic Forum**, evaluates gender equality across nations using various indices and is considered a crucial tool for assessing global progress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Gender Gap Report:**

 
 
• The **Global Gender Gap Report** was first introduced by the **World Economic Forum** in **2006**.
 
• It measures gender equality across four dimensions: **Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment**.
 
• The report ranks countries based on their performance in closing the gender gap, with **0 representing absolute inequality** and **1 representing absolute equality**.
 
• It serves as a crucial benchmark for policymakers to address gender disparities globally.

• Iceland has a **mandatory parental leave policy**, where both parents are entitled to three months of leave, ensuring shared parenting responsibilities.
 
• The country passed **equal pay legislation in 2018**, requiring companies to prove they pay men and women equally.
 
• Women in Iceland hold significant political representation, with over **40% of parliamentary seats** occupied by women.
 
• Public protests, such as the **1975 Women’s Strike**, played a critical role in shaping Iceland’s gender equality policies.

• **Norway:** Known for its robust policies on gender equality, including strong parental leave and workplace equality programs.
 
• **Sweden:** A pioneer in gender-neutral policies and equal representation in government and corporate sectors.
 
• **Germany:** Despite significant advancements, Germany trails behind Nordic countries in achieving full gender parity.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Gender Equality:**
 
 
• Gender equality is essential for achieving **sustainable development** and ensuring social justice.
 
• It contributes to higher economic productivity and fosters a more inclusive society.
 
• Eliminating gender disparities is crucial for achieving global goals like the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5**, which focuses on gender equality.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Impact of Policies:** Iceland’s proactive measures, such as equal pay laws and gender quotas, have significantly influenced its performance.
 
• **Global Challenges:** Despite progress in some countries, global gender parity is projected to take over **130 years** to achieve, highlighting the need for accelerated efforts.

• The book explores themes of **human connection, identity, and resilience**, resonating deeply with readers and critics alike.

__
 
• **About the Pulitzer Prize:**

 
 
• The Pulitzer Prize was established in **1917** by provisions in the will of **Joseph Pulitzer**, a Hungarian-American journalist and newspaper publisher.
 
• It is administered by **Columbia University** in New York City and recognizes achievements in **journalism, literature, and musical composition**.
 
• The Fiction category specifically honors works of fiction by American authors, published in the preceding calendar year.
 
 
 
• **Criteria for the Pulitzer Prize in Fiction:**
 
 
• The work must be an original piece of fiction written by an **American author**.
 
• It should exhibit **excellence in prose**, character development, and thematic depth.
 
• Preference is given to works that deal with **American life and culture**.

• **2015:** "All the Light We Cannot See" by Anthony Doerr - A story set during World War II about a blind French girl and a German boy.
 
• **2007:** "The Road" by Cormac McCarthy - A post-apocalyptic tale of a father and son’s journey.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Winning the Pulitzer Prize:**
 
 
• Winning the Pulitzer elevates the author's visibility and critical acclaim.
 
• The prize often leads to increased book sales and wider readership.
 
• It is considered one of the most prestigious awards in American literature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nomination and Selection Process:**

 
 
• Entries are submitted by publishers, and a jury of distinguished writers and critics evaluates the submissions.
 
• The jury selects finalists and sends their recommendations to the Pulitzer Prize Board, which makes the final decision.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility:**
 
 
• To be eligible, the work must be published in the United States during the award year.
 
• The author must be an American citizen.
 
 
 
• **Other Categories of Pulitzer Prizes:**
 
 
• **Journalism:** Includes awards for investigative reporting, public service, and feature writing.
 
• **Music:** Recognizes distinguished compositions by American composers.
 
• **Drama:** Honors plays that depict American life.
